notable_absence.finding: The example response on this page returns TWO distinct arrays: `expired_backups` and `expired_backups_with_non_expired_dependents`. The field name strongly implies the Backup Service tracks, and treats differently, expired backups that still have non-expired incremental backups depending on them - directly paralleling backup-delete-backups.json's disable_safe_remove_check dependency guard and this batch's confirmed backup:full-backup/backup:incremental-backup dependency chain. But the page supplies only the field name and one example value, with no prose explaining what happens differently to a backup in that second category (is it excluded from automatic pruning? does it require disable_safe_remove_check to prune?). No sentence exists to quote for a relation, so none is asserted - named here instead, per the instruction not to silently drop an interesting but unquotable structural signal.

cross_component_finding: port:8097 being introduced only NOW, on this batch's 8th of 11 files despite the number 8097 appearing in literally every preceding page's curl examples, is itself a small methodological finding: an extraction agent reading pages in isolation could easily have minted port:8097 on file 1 from a bare URL number with much weaker evidence, or never minted it at all if no page stated the port's purpose in prose. This page's explicit framing sentence - 'These URIs are only available from the Backup Service port (8097 by default) on nodes running the Backup Service' - is the ONLY sentence in this batch that names the port as a first-class fact rather than an incidental part of an example URL, which is why it is the mint point chosen here.
